title: Flaming sky over Paranal
caption: Red airglow over the VLT Auxiliary Telescopes, Paranal Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at Paranal Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: Three of the four Auxiliary Telescopes of ESO's Very Large Telescope stand in a ghostly scene at Paranal Observatory. Behind them, the quiet Atacama sky glows with a red shimmer that looks almost like an aurora.

That shimmer is airglow. It comes from chemical reactions high in the atmosphere that give off light. Usually these emissions are fairly weak, but on the night this photo was taken they were much brighter than normal.

Each Auxiliary Telescope has a mirror 1.8 metres across. They are designed to work alongside one another as if they were a single telescope, combining their light through the VLT Interferometer. Working together in this way lets the set of telescopes pick out finer detail than any one of them could manage by itself.

understand.summary: This is a landscape photograph taken with a camera at an ESO site, in visible light. The camera settings and colour processing are not published.
understand.eye: Airglow is normally hard for the eye to see, but a long camera exposure gathers enough light to bring out its red colour, and on this night the glow was unusually strong.
